Test the full model of each gene

Source: R/sc.p.vector.R
sc.p.vector.Rd

sc.p.vector() fits the full polynomial model of each gene to its pseudo-bulk counts and tests it against the intercept-only model. The genes whose adjusted p-value is at most p_value have a non-flat profile; sc.t.fit() selects the terms of their models.

sc.p.vector(
  scmpObj,
  p_value = 0.05,
  mt_correction = "BH",
  min_na = 6,
  min_counts = 0,
  min_bins_expressed = 0,
  family = negative.binomial(theta = 10, link = link),
  epsilon = 1e-08,
  verbose = TRUE,
  offset = TRUE,
  max_it = 100,
  link = "log",
  theta_estimate = "none",
  test = "chisq",
  BPPARAM = SerialParam()
)

Arguments

scmpObj

A ScMaSigPro object.

p_value

The level of the adjusted p-values: the genes at or below it have a non-flat profile. It is also the default level of sc.t.fit().

mt_correction

The method of stats::p.adjust() that adjusts the p-values for multiple testing; "BH" is that of Benjamini and Hochberg (1995).

min_na

The minimum number of bins with a value (not NA) that a gene needs to be fitted, as min.obs of p.vector() in maSigPro. Only counts with missing values, such as microarray data given to create_scmp() with use_as_bin = TRUE, have fewer; it can be at most the number of bins of the design.

min_counts

Minimum total count of a gene, summed over the bins of the design. Genes with fewer counts are left out of the fit. The default, 0, keeps every gene.

min_bins_expressed

Minimum number of bins of the design in which a gene has a count above 0. Genes expressed in fewer bins are left out of the fit. The default, 0, keeps every gene; it can be at most the number of bins.

family

The distribution of the error term, a stats::family() object: by default the negative binomial with theta = 10 and the link link. A family given here keeps its own link.

epsilon

The convergence tolerance of stats::glm().

verbose

Whether to print progress messages.

offset

Whether to add the offset of each bin, the logarithm of its size factor (see Details), to the linear predictor; it needs the log link.

max_it

The maximum number of iterations of stats::glm().

link

The link of the default family: "log", the model of the paper, or "identity". When family is given, link must be its link. The identity link needs offset = FALSE; under it the fitted mean of a gene can become negative, and stats::glm() then warns.

theta_estimate

For a negative binomial family: "none" (the default) fits every gene with the theta of family (10 by default, as maSigPro). "gene" estimates theta by maximum likelihood on each gene's full model and fits the gene with it; "global" fits every gene with the median of these estimates. The estimates are kept in the distribution parameter, for sc.t.fit() and plotDiagnostics(): theta_gene holds one per gene and theta_estimate the choice.

test

The test of each gene's full model against its intercept-only model: "chisq" (the default) or "F". Both divide the difference in deviance between the two models by the dispersion of the full model, which, for the negative binomial and Gaussian families, is estimated as its Pearson statistic divided by its residual degrees of freedom. "chisq" compares the result with the chi-squared distribution, as maSigPro does. "F" also divides it by the difference in degrees of freedom and compares it with the F distribution on the residual degrees of freedom of the full model: the F test of stats::anova.glm(). With the Gaussian family both values give the F test, the test of maSigPro for that family. "F" needs a family whose dispersion is estimated, so not stats::binomial() or stats::poisson(). The value is kept in the test parameter. See Details.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallelParam object that runs the per-gene fits, such as BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(2) (Linux and macOS) or BiocParallel::SnowParam(2) (any system). The default, BiocParallel::SerialParam(), fits the genes one after another; create it with progressbar = TRUE for a progress bar. The results do not depend on the backend.

Value

The object with the p-values and the genes with a non-flat profile in the Profile slot (class VariableProfiles), the offsets in the Design slot and the settings of the fit in the Parameters slot.

Details

With offset = TRUE, the fits include an offset as Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.3 and Supplementary Section S1.3, describe it: "scMaSigPro incorporates an offset value to the Poly-GLM model to adjust for disparities in total read counts per bin. This offset is calculated as the logarithm of size factors for each bin". The size factors are those of the median-of-ratios method (Anders and Huber 2010; Love et al. 2014) on the raw counts: "The size factor for each bin is the median of the ratios of its counts to the geometric means for each gene". Only the genes with a count above 0 in every bin enter the medians, and the fit stops when there is none: fewer, larger bins (sc.squeeze()) or offset = FALSE avoid it. The genes are fitted on their raw counts, without a pseudo-count: "scMaSigPro can directly process raw counts". The offsets are stored in the Design slot, where sc.t.fit() finds them.

Genes are left out of the fit when they have fewer than min_na values, when all their counts are zero, and when they are below min_counts or min_bins_expressed. They have no p-value and do not count in the multiple-testing correction; scmpResults() gives them NA. The size factors are computed before min_counts and min_bins_expressed are applied, so these two filters change the results of the genes they keep only through the correction.

The test of the full model is the first step of the method of Srivastava et al. (2024), Section 2.4: "scMaSigPro implements a two-step strategy similar to the maSigPro method", in which the full model of each gene is "evaluated against a simpler intercept-only model via hypothesis testing based on the log-likelihood ratio statistic". The default, test = "chisq", is that test as maSigPro computes it for families other than the Gaussian: the statistic is divided by the estimated dispersion and compared with the chi-squared distribution, as if the dispersion were known. With few bins, and so few residual degrees of freedom, the estimate varies from gene to gene and the test calls more genes significant than its level. test = "F", the quasi-likelihood F test, accounts for the estimation of the dispersion through the residual degrees of freedom of the F distribution.

Examples

data("scmp.ob", package = "scMaSigPro")
# Test the full model of every gene with the F test
scmp <- sc.p.vector(scmp.ob, test = "F", verbose = FALSE)
sum(scmpResults(scmp)$non_flat)
#> [1] 43
